mappings.note: Short circuiting versus overloading - LO-7.
Why a short circuit sparks and why the spark is white - LO-7's short circuit.
Asks for both rules by name and statement - the right-hand thumb rule and Fleming's left-hand rule, which are precisely the two rules LO-5 names. A clean single-code hit.
Non-intersection of field lines and the parallel-equidistant representation of a uniform field - both LO-6.
Iron filings around a bar magnet, closed curves and strength at the poles - LO-6.
Earth wire, short circuiting and fuse ratings - three LO-7 topics in one question.
Identify which of two bars is a magnet by tapping one. Permanent-magnet behaviour; no outcome fits. Goal level. Frame gap.
Moving a bar magnet near a solenoid sets up an induced current - electromagnetic induction, LO-2. Not LO-4: the coil is the detector here, not the source of the field.
Parts (i) and (ii) are bar-magnet field-line direction and crowding (LO-6); part (iii) is an advantage of A.C. (LO-7). Split because the question genuinely spans two outcomes.
Detecting the central field of a circular loop (LO-4) and naming the rule that predicts its direction (LO-5).
Galvanometer deflects when a magnet is pushed in or withdrawn and not when it is held still - flux change induces a current, LO-2.
Lists the ways of inducing a current in a coil - LO-2's induction.
Electric meter, earthing and overloading precautions - LO-7.

Two ways to induce a current, when the induced current is largest, and Fleming's right-hand rule for its direction. LO-2 names that rule, so this stays whole rather than splitting to LO-5, which names the left-hand rule.
General precautions in the use of electricity - the safety half of LO-7.
Mark the polarity of each solenoid face and draw the internal field lines (LO-6's named object), then give two ways to raise the field (LO-4).
Centre-zero galvanometer, magnet moved towards and away, and coil and magnet moved together so no relative motion - LO-2's flux change.
Heating effect, fuse in series, and a domestic circuit diagram - LO-7 throughout.

Parts (i) and (iii) are bar-magnet field lines and crowding (LO-6); part (iv) is the A.C. frequency (LO-7). Part (ii) carries a wrong printed key ('Oersted' given as the SI unit of B) - flagged as a bank defect.
Name and state both direction rules - identical in substance to the 3-mark item 147 and mapped identically.

Fuse definition, material, wiring, ratings and function are LO-7; part (iv) computes a fuse rating from 1 kW at 220 V, which is C 2.4's current/voltage mathematisation and has no outcome inside this chapter's frame.
Electromagnet: soft-iron core, how it is made, how to strengthen it. Filed on LO-4's solenoid because the frame has no electromagnet outcome.
Inducing a current with a moving magnet plus mutual induction between two coils on make and break - LO-2.
D.C. and A.C. current-time graphs, sources, frequency and transmission; filed on LO-7 for want of an A.C./D.C. outcome - recorded.
